principles: Make convergence-stall a mechanical signal, not a relied-on convention.
Soft over hard: warn and suggest escalation; never block a transition the operator may legitimately need.
Reuse existing round/blocking helpers; do not duplicate the round-count or blocking logic.
Stay bounded: warn only — defer the larger per-round cost-reduction (targeted re-review) to a separate story.
drivers: REVIEW rounds re-trigger on every source-changing fix commit, and there is no mechanical signal when rounds stop converging.
An operator who keeps fixing minor findings instead of dismissing them can livelock with no warning.
All inputs already exist (round count from events, per-round findings), so a detector is cheap and additive.

options.name: Option C: soft advisory-only stall detector
pros: Gives an escalation hint exactly when a story is stuck.
cons: Does not reduce the number of rounds (it only warns).
Trend heuristic must be tuned to avoid false alarms on healthy convergence.

options.name: Option A: raw round-count ceiling warning
cons: False-alarms on a healthy decreasing series (e.g. R1->R2->R3 with findings shrinking to 0).

options.name: Option B: targeted/partial re-review
pros: Actually reduces per-round reviewer cost by only re-running affected dimensions.
cons: Larger change with real under-review risk (could skip a reviewer that should re-check).
Out of scope here; deferred to a separate story.

chosen: Option C: soft advisory-only stall detector
rationale: Option C closes the missing mechanical signal with a minimal, additive, non-blocking advisory that reuses existing round/blocking helpers. Option A is rejected because a raw ceiling false-alarms on healthy convergence. Option B genuinely reduces round cost but is a larger, higher-risk change and is recorded as deferred to a separate story. C is the proportionate first step.

preMortem.scenario: The detector fires on a healthy decreasing series and trains operators to ignore it.
preMortem.trigger: A raw round-count ceiling is used instead of a trend check.
preMortem.consequence: False alarms erode trust; the signal becomes noise.
preMortem.mitigation: Use a trend-based heuristic (no downward trend across the recent window) and cover a healthy-decreasing series as an explicit no-advisory smoke case.

preMortem.scenario: The advisory silently becomes a de-facto blocker.
preMortem.trigger: It is wired into a gate path or made to throw / affect the transition result.
preMortem.consequence: A story that legitimately needs more rounds gets stuck — the opposite of the intent.
preMortem.mitigation: Keep it pure stdout text appended after the transition succeeds; add a smoke asserting REVIEW->TEST still passes while the advisory is present.

preMortem.scenario: The detector duplicates round-count or blocking logic and drifts from the canonical rules.
preMortem.trigger: Reimplementing round counting or blocking-severity decay instead of importing the existing helpers.
preMortem.consequence: Two sources of truth diverge; the advisory disagrees with the real gate.
preMortem.mitigation: Import resolveReviewRoundCount + isFindingBlocking/effectiveBlockingSeverities from advisory.ts/guard-utils.ts; the per-round accessor only groups findings, it does not redefine blocking.
